key_claims: Four complementary regime-switching specifications all fail OOS on TAIFEX 2020-2021
Vol-normalized OFI crosses methodological |t|>2 (DM +2.25, AUC 0.594) but not Harvey |t|>3
Cross-market SPY/N225/TAIFEX gap² direction-consistent weak-universal signal
Methodological contribution: 4-branch honest-null protocol + regime-free alternative identification

subsections: Four specifications: tertile / spline / volnorm / expanding
2.2 Lee-Mykland jump detection (K=16 BV, Gumbel alpha=0.01, threshold 5.1256)
3.3 Descriptive stats (jump rates, VIX ranges, |OFI| tails)
4.1 Four-branch null evidence (Table 1 + Figure C AUC ranking)
4.4 Regime-switching rescue exhausted (MS-GAS parallel via K1133b)
5.2 Why all four VIX-conditional branches fail (structural IS/OOS disjunction)
5.3 Why vol-normalization partially succeeds (regime-free endogenous standardization)
5.4 Why partial positive is not fully positive (33 OOS jumps power ceiling)
5.5 Limitations (single market, Asia-Pacific, 33 jumps hard-bounded, binary target, VIX-only)

key_takeaways: For crisis-era OOS data, regime-conditional specifications structurally susceptible to support disjunction
Regime-free adaptive standardization is cleaner better-identified alternative
Cross-market weak-universal corroboration supports the methodological claim
Honest-null + partial-positive framing is appropriate at 33-OOS-jump power ceiling
